# Lighting, Shadowing & Relighting

Also called: 3DGS Lighting, Gaussian Splatting Shading, Deferred Gaussian Rendering, T_light Self-Shadowing

## Overview
This family extends 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) rendering to support dynamic, physically-based lighting and self-occlusion. Standard 3DGS bakes lighting into spherical harmonics (SH) or uses fixed forward shading, preventing real-time environment changes or accurate shadows [3459-analytic-splatting-forward-shading.md]. These methods solve that by either deferring material attributes to a G-buffer for split-sum environment map integration [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md] or by performing a dedicated light-space rasterization pass to compute front-facing transmittance for self-shadowing [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on 3D Gaussian primitives defined by mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$ (or scales and orientation), opacity $o$, and color $\mathbf{c}$ (or spherical harmonic coefficients). The core challenge is computing the pixel color $C$ and accumulated alpha $\alpha$ given a camera ray. Standard splatting projects 3D Gaussians to 2D ellipses, computes a 2D alpha mask, and blends them in screen space. These models modify the blending or shading stage: some refine the depth metric used for sorting, others integrate the 3D density function directly along the ray, and others use weighted averages to bypass sorting. All assume the Gaussians are sorted or processed in a manner that approximates front-to-back accumulation to ensure correct occlusion.

For relighting, splats must carry physical material attributes: normal, roughness, reflectance (specular strength), and albedo (diffuse color) [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md]. These are stored in a parallel Material Buffer aligned with the Splat Buffer [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].

For self-shadowing, a virtual "sun camera" is constructed to simulate a directional light source [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md]. This camera is placed at a large distance with a narrow field of view (FOV) to minimize parallax error to below 2% [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

Both relighting (for cache locality) and shadowing (for correct front-to-back accumulation) require sorting. Relighting uses spatial locality algorithms like Morton codes [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md]. Shadowing sorts Gaussians by depth relative to the sun camera [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

During the light pass for shadowing, the projection covariance is not expanded by $0.3I$ and no amplitude compensation is applied, preserving the main camera pass's sampling expansion [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md]. In shadowing calculations, sun camera framing, sorting, coverage, and threshold branches are treated as constants to prevent incorrect gradient propagation [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

## Subtopics

### [Ref-Gaussian Deferred Surfel Rendering with Split-Sum IBL](4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md)
A real-time deferred shading method for relighting 3DGS on mobile hardware. It solves dynamic environment lighting by decomposing splats into PBR materials (albedo, normal, roughness, reflectance) and using split-sum IBL. Unlike forward-shading methods that bake lighting, it allows real-time environment swapping without retraining. Choose this for dynamic, physically-based relighting on constrained hardware.

### [3D Gaussian Splatting Self-Shadowing (T_light)](4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t-light.md)
Calculates self-shadowing transmittance $T_{light}$ via a dedicated light-space rasterization pass. It sets itself apart by accumulating depth-weighted transmittance without modifying the primary camera's covariance expansion, ensuring consistency with the main render pass. Choose this for accurate self-occlusion in static or dynamic scenes.

### [Light Space Rasterization for T_light](4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t-light.md)
Computes $T_{light}$ using light-space rasterization. It differs from voxel-based fallbacks by providing full continuous gradients and zero parameter expansion, enabling differentiable relighting. Choose this when differentiable training or high-fidelity gradient-based optimization is required.

## Background
Originating from the need to overcome the limitations of baked spherical harmonics in 3D Gaussian Splatting [3459-analytic-splatting-forward-shading.md], these methods were developed to support dynamic lighting and self-shadowing. The deferred surfel approach targets mobile real-time performance [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md], while the $T_{light}$ methods address the lack of self-occlusion in standard splatting [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md]. They are used in high-fidelity 3D reconstruction viewers, mobile AR/VR applications, and differentiable rendering pipelines.
